## Beads Issue Tracker

Use Beads (`bd`) for durable task tracking in repositories that include it. Use the `beads` skill at `.agents/skills/beads/SKILL.md` (project install) or `~/.agents/skills/beads/SKILL.md` (global install) for Beads workflow guidance, then use the `bd` CLI for issue operations.

### Quick Reference

```bash
bd ready                # Find available work
bd show <id>            # View issue details
bd update <id> --claim  # Claim work
bd close <id>           # Complete work
bd prime                # Refresh Beads context
```

### Rules

- Use `bd` for all task tracking; do not create markdown TODO lists.
- Run `bd prime` when Beads context is missing or stale. Codex 0.129.0+ can load Beads context automatically through native hooks; use `/hooks` to inspect or toggle them.
- Keep persistent project memory in Beads via `bd remember`; do not create ad hoc memory files.

**Architecture in one line:** issues live in a local Dolt DB; sync uses `refs/dolt/data` on your git remote; `.beads/issues.jsonl` is a passive export. See https://github.com/gastownhall/beads/blob/main/docs/SYNC_CONCEPTS.md for details and anti-patterns.

## Project Operating Rules

### Load only the context the work needs

- Start with `bd prime`, `bd ready`, and the project-local `beads` skill.
- Read `docs/project-charter.md` before adding features, commands, integrations, schemas, or other project surface area.
- Read `docs/product/brief.md` and `docs/product/requirements.md` before changing user-visible behavior.
- Read `docs/architecture/README.md` and `docs/architecture/boundaries.md` before changing dependencies, data ownership, interfaces, trust boundaries, or deployment structure.
- Read `docs/quality.md` before implementation and `docs/ways-of-working.md` before handoff.
- Follow more specific repository instructions when they exist; do not load unrelated documents merely because they are available.

### Respect scope and boundaries

- Tie new work to an explicit user outcome and confirm that it belongs within the project charter.
- Prefer extending an owned interface over bypassing a boundary or leaking implementation details across it.
- Stop and ask the user when scope, architecture, irreversible operations, security, privacy, cost, or conflicting instructions require a human decision. Record the decision in the relevant durable document.

### Track durable work in Beads

- Beads is the source of truth for initiatives, tasks, blockers, dependencies, discoveries, and multi-session handoff; do not maintain parallel markdown task lists.
- Use epics for initiatives and child issues for testable increments. Include acceptance criteria and design notes when they affect execution.
- Check `bd ready`, inspect the issue, and claim it before substantial work.
- Record newly discovered work as a linked `discovered-from` issue instead of silently expanding scope.
- Use non-interactive commands. Never use `bd edit`; use `bd update` flags or stdin/body files for complex text.

### Build and validate safely

- Use the canonical commands in `docs/quality.md`; do not invent alternate build, test, migration, or release paths when the project defines one.
- Isolate tests from production data, user state, global configuration, credentials, external services, and real repositories unless the test explicitly requires and safely controls them.
- Update tests and durable documentation when behavior changes. If an applicable quality gate cannot run or is already broken, report it and create or update a Beads issue rather than hiding it.

### Keep architecture and agent behavior durable

- Use the project-local `likec4-dsl` skill before editing LikeC4 sources. Create views in `docs/architecture/model/` when visuals clarify multiple components, dependencies, data flow, deployment or trust boundaries, or a consequential decision.
- Record costly or durable architecture choices in `docs/decisions/`.
- Capture concise project rules outside this managed block. Put explained behaviors in `docs/agent-behaviors.md` and reusable specialized workflows in `.agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`.
- Never modify vendor-managed skills such as `beads` or `likec4-dsl` to store project policy.

### Complete and hand off

- Treat “let's wrap up,” “wrap up this session,” “prepare a handoff,” “land the plane,” and clear variations as explicit triggers to run the complete session wrap-up in `docs/ways-of-working.md`; do not merely summarize the conversation.
- Before finishing, capture follow-up work, run applicable quality gates, update durable documents, and close only issues whose acceptance criteria are met.
- Report changed files, validation results, issue status, blockers, and the next concrete action.
- End a triggered wrap-up with a self-contained, copy-pasteable prompt for a new agent session. Include the Beads issue, current state, next action, blockers or decisions needed, validation already performed, and the files or documents to read first.
- Do not commit, push, sync, publish, deploy, or perform destructive cleanup unless the user or an explicit repository policy authorizes it.
